rationale:
Evidence from iteration 2 (60 trials): kp 1.5 to 3.0 to 5.0 raised progress on every track (oval 0.12 to 0.47 to 0.71, s-bend 0.04 to 0.16 to 0.37, slalom 0.03 to 0.10 to 0.21). Two of 60 runs finished, both on the oval. Every other run left the tape at max_error of about 0.061 to 0.062 m, the 0.06 m limit, with about one line-loss event per run. Steering oscillation is 0.23 to 0.29 on the bends, up from about 0.07 at kp 1.5, so the loop is now oscillating as well as lagging. The failure is still a loss of the line at bends, and it has not been a jitter problem.

Diagnosis: the sensors sit only 0.04 m from the centre and 0.05 m ahead of the axle. That gives the controller little look-ahead and little lateral reach, so by the time the signal reacts the robot is already near the edge. The 0.12 m track and 0.8 kg mass also make the robot slow to turn for a given PWM difference.

Changes in this candidate:
(1) Sensors moved further forward to y = 0.08 m (the allowed maximum) for more look-ahead, so steering starts earlier and the lag that causes overshoot shrinks.
(2) Lateral spread widened to x = -0.06, -0.03, 0, 0.03, 0.06 m, so a sensor still sees tape at larger offsets. Weights stay -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 so that the signal scale stays proportional to offset.
(3) wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10 m, so the same PWM difference produces a larger turn rate.
(4) mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg, lowering yaw inertia so the robot turns faster and can correct in time.
(5) kd 0.5 to 1.0, to damp the oscillation that appeared at kp 5 now that the look-ahead is longer.
(6) kp 5.0 to 5.5, a small increase, since the wider sensor spread already raises the signal per unit offset.
(7) base_speed held at 1.0 so that the change in response can be read without a speed change. body_width is unchanged, because the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m for any allowed body width.

Expected result: fewer off-track exits at bends, progress above 0.6 on all three tracks, and steering_oscillation at or below about 0.25 despite the higher kd. Hypotheses: H1, the forward sensors and wider spread reduce line loss at bends, shown by line_loss_events falling below 0.9. H2, the lighter, narrower robot turns faster, shown by higher progress on the s-bend and slalom at the same speed. H3, kd 1.0 damps the oscillation, shown by steering_oscillation falling from the iteration-2 level. Next measurements: progress and completion_time to see whether speed or stability limits the score, max_error and line_loss_events for stability, steering_oscillation for damping, and control_effort for gain cost.
